zh: 月如收拾了床辅，又洗了手，然后开楼门叫丫头从厨房里将一锅鸭粥端了来。随即遣走丫头，亲手盛了一碗捧给胡雪岩，她自己也盛了半碗，在一旁相陪。“老爷，”月如闲闲问道：“是不是说二十三家的管总，要来个大扳位？”“是啊！老唐到德清就是商量这件事去的。”“你预备把老唐调到哪里？”“这还不晓得。”“怎么你会不晓得呢？”“ ‘凭天断’，我怎么会晓得？”“啥叫‘凭天娄’？”“抽签。”胡雪岩答说：“二十三家典当分做大中小三等，分等抽签。譬如顶大的有八家，这八家的管总合在一起抽签，抽到哪里是哪里。““这样说，老唐抽到苏州到苏州，抽到镇江到镇江？”“不错。”
en: Yueru straightened the bedding and washed her hands, then opened the door to the stairs and called the maid to bring up the pot of duck congee. She sent the maid away again, filled a bowl for Hu, and took half a bowl herself to keep him company. “Master,” she asked casually, “is it true that you mean to move all twenty-three managers to different shops?” “Yes. That is what Old Tang has gone to Deqing to discuss.” “Where do you mean to send him?” “I do not know yet.” “How can you not know?” “Heaven will decide. How could I know?” “What do you mean, Heaven will decide?” “We shall draw lots. The twenty-three pawnshops will be divided into three classes—large, medium, and small—and the managers will draw within each class. Suppose there are eight in the largest class: their eight managers draw together, and each goes wherever his lot sends him.” “Then if Old Tang draws Suzhou he goes to Suzhou, and if he draws Zhenjiang he goes to Zhenjiang?” “Exactly.”

zh: 听得这话，月如将筷子一放，掩着脸踉踉跄跄地奔回卧室。胡雪岩大吃一惊，随即也跟了进去，只见她伏在床上，双肩耸动着在哭。“月如，月如！”他尽管推着她的身子，她却不理，但哭声仿佛止住了。“你到底为啥？无事端端地哭得好伤心。”“我怎么不要伤心？”月如脸朝里床口发怨言：“你死没良心！把我骗到手，尝过新鲜了，马上想这么一个法子！叫老唐带着我充军充到外县，你好眼不见为净！”“这是从哪里说起？”胡雪岩不由得失笑，“我做梦也没有想到，你会把毫不相干的两桩事情扯在一起！”“哪里是毫不相干？老唐调到外县，我自然要跟了去，你好象一点都不在乎，玩过就算数了。“这番指摘，不能说她没有道理，胡雪岩细想了一会说道：“你也不一定要跟老唐去，我替你另外买一幢房子。”“做你的小公馆？”“也不是啥小公馆……”胡雪岩有些词穷了，月如却毫不放松。“不是小公馆是啥呢？”她说：“就算作为是老唐买的房子，我一个人住在杭州，别人问起来，我怎么回复人家？而且你要来了，总归有人晓得的，跟你的人不说，自然会有人到螺蛳太太面前去说，总有一天带了人打上门来。那时候我除了投河跳井，没有第二条路好走。“话说得驳不倒，胡雪岩愣了好半晌说：“月如，你晓得的，二十三家管总调动的事在前，我们今天会睡在一床，是我连昨天都没有想到的事。本来是两桩不搭界的事情，现在倒好象扯在一起了。你倒说说看，有啥好办法？”
en: At this, Yueru put down her chopsticks, covered her face, and stumbled back into the bedroom. Startled, Hu followed. She lay face down on the bed, her shoulders shaking with sobs. “Yueru! Yueru!” Though he kept nudging her, she paid no attention. The sound of her crying did seem to stop. “What is the matter? Why are you suddenly so heartbroken?” Facing the inner side of the bed, she complained, “How could I not be? You heartless creature! You have tricked me into your arms, had your taste of something new, and immediately thought of this scheme. You will have Old Tang take me into exile in another county, so you need never set eyes on me again!” Hu could not help laughing in astonishment. “Where did that come from? I never dreamed you would connect two things that have nothing to do with each other.” “Nothing to do with each other? If Old Tang is sent away, I must go with him. You do not seem to care in the least. You have had your pleasure, and that is the end of it.” Her accusation was not wholly unreasonable. After considering it, Hu said, “You need not necessarily go with him. I could buy you another house.” “To be your secret household?” “It would not exactly be that…” He was at a loss, but Yueru pressed on. “What else would it be? Even if we said Old Tang had bought it, how should I explain living alone in Hangzhou? People would ask. And someone would be sure to discover your visits. If your attendants said nothing, somebody else would tell Madam Luosi. One day she would come with a crowd to attack me. Then I should have no choice but to throw myself into a river or a well.” Unable to refute her, Hu stood speechless for some time. “You know the transfer plan came first. Even yesterday I had no idea we would share a bed today. The two things were entirely separate; now they seem tied together. Tell me, then: what can we do?”

zh: 月如故意沉吟了一会，方始说道：“办法是有。先要问你，你是只想今天捡捡便宜呢，还是仍旧要我？”“仍旧要你。”“那就只有一个办法，原样不动。”“怎么叫原样不动？”“别家的管总，你尽管去调动，老唐仍旧管公济，”月如又说：“老唐是帮你管典当的头脑，跟别家不同，他不动是说得过去的。”“那怎么说得过去？一有了例外，大家不服。”“那就大家不动。”月如又说：“我是不懂做生意，不过照我想，做生意全靠人头熟，忽然之间到了陌生地方，两只眼睛墨黑，等到你看清楚，生意已经让别家抢走了。”胡雪岩心里七上八下，盘算来盘算去，苦无兼顾的善策，最后叹口气说：“只好大家不动。”
en: Yueru deliberately paused as though thinking it over. “There is a way. But first I must ask: did you only want to take advantage of me today, or do you still want me?” “I still want you.” “Then there is only one thing to do. Leave everything as it is.” “What do you mean?” “Move the other managers wherever you please, but leave Old Tang at Gongji. He is the head of all your pawnshop managers, different from the others. There is good reason to leave him where he is.” “How could that be justified? Once I make an exception, everyone will object.” “Then move none of them. I know nothing about business, but surely it depends on knowing people. Arrive suddenly in a strange place and you are completely in the dark. By the time you can see your way, other firms have taken the business.” Hu turned the matter over anxiously, unable to find a solution that served both purposes. At last he sighed. “We shall have to leave everyone where he is.”

zh: 唐子韶的“美人计”，元宝街的下人很快地都知道了，不过胡老太太治家极严，将“来说是非者，便是是非人”这句俗语，奉为金科玉律，所以没有人敢到十二楼去说这个秘密。但近处未传，远处却传到了。古应春以抑郁的语气，将这件事告诉了七姑奶奶，而七姑奶奶不信。“小爷叔不是这种人。如果为了女人会把生意上商量好的事推翻不算，小爷叔哪里会有今天这种场面，老早败下来了。”“我懒得跟你争。好在他就要来接左大人，你不妨当面问问他。”“我当然要当面问他。”七姑奶奶继续为胡雪岩辩护，“二十三家典当管总仍然照旧，一走有他的道理。小爷叔的打算不会错的。”第二天，胡雪岩就到了，仍旧住在古家，应酬到半夜十一点多种才跟古应春一起回家。七姑奶奶照例预备了消夜在等他们。把杯闲谈之际，七姑奶奶闲闲问道：“小爷叔，你二十三家典当管总调动的计划，听说打消了，是为啥？”“嗐，七姐，请你不要问了。”一听这话，七姑奶奶勃然变色，立即问说：“为啥不要问？”“七姐，有趣的事，大家谈谈，没趣的事谈起来，连带你也不高兴，何苦？”“这样说，是真的了。真的姓唐的做了圈套，请你胡大先生去钻。小爷叔，你怎么会做这种糊涂事？”
en: The servants in Yuanbao Street soon knew of Tang Zishao’s beauty trap. Hu’s mother, however, ruled the household strictly. She treated the saying “Those who bring you gossip are troublemakers themselves” as an inviolable law, so no one dared carry this secret into the Twelve Chambers. It remained unspoken nearby but traveled far away. Gu related it gloomily to the Seventh Lady, who refused to believe him. “Little Uncle is not that sort of man. If a woman could make him overturn a settled business plan, how could he have built up what he has today? He would have ruined himself long ago.” “I cannot be bothered to argue. He will soon be here to meet His Excellency Zuo. Ask him yourself.” “Of course I shall.” She continued defending Hu. “He must have his reasons for leaving the twenty-three managers in place. His judgment will not be wrong.” Hu arrived the next day and stayed, as before, at Gu’s house. He and Gu returned from their engagements after eleven that night to find the Seventh Lady waiting with the customary late supper. Over wine and conversation, she asked casually, “Little Uncle, I hear you have abandoned your plan to transfer the twenty-three managers. Why?” “Ah, Seventh Sister, please do not ask.” Her expression changed at once. “Why should I not ask?” “Pleasant things are worth talking about. Unpleasant things will only upset you as well. Why bother?” “Then it is true. Tang really did lay a trap for you to walk into. Little Uncle, how could you do anything so foolish?”

zh: 说到“糊涂”二字，嘴已经歪了，眼睛也斜了，脸红如火，古应春叫声：“不好！”赶紧上前去扶，七姑奶奶已在凳子上坐不住，一头栽在地上，幸好地上铺了极厚的波斯羊毛地毯，头没有摔破。“是中风！”胡雪岩跳起身来喊道：“来人！”于是一面叫进人来，扶起七姑奶奶，一面打发人去延医，胡雪岩关照去请在咸丰年间曾入宫“请脉”，号称太医的曹郎中，但古应春相信西医，且有一个熟识的医生，名叫艾礼脱，所以另外派人去请。时已夜半，叩门将医生从床上叫起来，自然得费些工夫。古应春倒还沉得住气，反是胡雪岩异样地焦急不安，望着躺在软榻上，闭着眼“呼噜、呼噜”只在喉间作痰响的七姑奶奶，搓着手蹀躞不停。他知道七姑奶奶是听到他做了没出息的事，气恼过度，致生此变。倘或不治，则“我虽不杀伯仁，伯仁由我而死”，会一辈子歉疚在心，日子还过得下去？
en: As she said “foolish,” her mouth twisted, her eyes turned askew, and her face became fiery red. “Something is wrong!” Gu cried, rushing to support her. She could no longer sit upright and fell headlong from her stool. Fortunately, the thick Persian wool carpet kept her head from being cut open. “A stroke!” Hu jumped up and shouted for servants. While some lifted her, others were sent for doctors. Hu ordered them to fetch Doctor Cao, known as an imperial physician because he had been summoned to take pulses in the palace during the Xianfeng reign. Gu trusted Western medicine and sent separately for a doctor he knew, Ailituo. It was past midnight, and knocking up doctors from their beds naturally took time. Gu remained comparatively composed; Hu was extraordinarily distressed. He paced and wrung his hands, watching the Seventh Lady on the couch, her eyes closed, a rattling sound of phlegm in her throat. He knew that anger at his disgraceful conduct had brought this on. If she died, it would be like the saying, “I did not kill Boren, but Boren died because of me.” Lifelong remorse would be his. How could he go on living with it?

zh: 好不容易将医生等到了，先来的是艾礼脱，一看七姑奶奶躺在那里，用英语跟古应春说中风的病人，不宜横卧。古应春随即叫两名仆妇，把七姑奶奶扶了起来，靠在安乐椅上、左右扶持。西医看病，没有“男女授受不亲”那一套，艾礼脱打开皮包，取出听诊器挂在耳朵上，关照古应春解开七姑奶奶的衣钮，拿听筒按在她胸前听心跳。诊断完了，撬开牙关，用温开水设法将他带来的药丸，让她吞了下去。然后告诉古应春，六小时以后，如能苏醒，性命可保，他天亮后再来复诊。正在谈着，曹郎中到了，艾礼脱脸色不大好看，抗议式地对古应春说，看西医就不能看中医。这一下，让古应春为难了，跟胡雪岩商量，应该怎么办。“你相信西医，自然是你作主。曹郎中，病情他照看，方子由他照开，不吃他的药就是了。”“不错，不错！这法子好。”古应春照他的话办。
en: At last Ailituo arrived. Seeing her lying flat, he told Gu in English that a stroke patient should not be left in that position. Gu immediately had two serving women sit her up in an armchair, supporting her on either side. Western doctors observed none of the rules against physical contact between the sexes. Ailituo opened his bag, put the stethoscope to his ears, and had Gu unfasten her clothes so that he could listen to her heart. After examining her, he pried open her clenched teeth and contrived to get her to swallow a pill with warm water. If she regained consciousness after six hours, he told Gu, her life could be saved. He would return after daybreak. As he was speaking, Doctor Cao arrived. Ailituo looked displeased and protested that someone receiving Western treatment could not also consult a Chinese physician. Gu was embarrassed and asked Hu what to do. “You trust Western medicine, so naturally you must decide. Let Doctor Cao examine her and write his prescription as usual. Simply do not give her his medicine.” “Quite right. That is the way.” Gu followed the suggestion.

zh: 艾礼脱的本领不错，到了天亮，七姑奶奶居然张开眼睛了，但胡雪岩去倦得眼不开眼睛。“小爷叔，你赶紧去睡一觉，下午还要去接左大人。”古应春说，“尽管放心去睡，到时候我会叫你。”“能放心睡得着倒好了。”“小爷叔，死生有命，而且看样子也好转了，你不必担心。”话虽如此，胡雪岩如何放心得下？双眼虽涩重得睁不开，睡却睡不好，时时惊醒，不到中午就起身了。“艾礼脱又来看病，说大致不要紧了，不过风瘫恐怕不免。带病延年，活上十几年的也多的是。”古应春说道：“小爷叔办正事去吧，可惜我不能陪你，见了左大人，代我说一声。”“好，好！我会说。”
en: Ailituo was a capable doctor. By daybreak the Seventh Lady had actually opened her eyes, though Hu was now too exhausted to keep his own open. “Little Uncle, go and sleep. You still have to meet His Excellency Zuo this afternoon. Rest without worrying; I shall wake you in time.” “If only I could put my mind at ease enough to sleep.” “Life and death are ordained. Besides, she seems better. You need not worry.” But how could Hu be easy? His eyes were sore and heavy, yet his sleep was broken by frequent starts. He rose before noon. “Ailituo has been again,” Gu told him. “He says the danger has largely passed, though paralysis is probably unavoidable. Many people live another ten years or more with such an illness. Attend to your business, Little Uncle. I am sorry I cannot accompany you. Please explain to His Excellency when you see him.” “Of course. I shall.”

zh: 左宗棠等过了慈禧太后的万寿，方始出京，奉准回籍扫墓，十一月二十五日到湖南省城长沙，第一件事是去拜访郭嵩焘。郭嵩焘与左宗棠有一段重重纠结的恩怨。当咸丰八年左宗棠在湖南巡抚骆秉章幕府中时，一切独断独行，一天骆秉章在签押房里看书。忽然听见辕门放铳，看辰光不是每天正午的“午时炮”，便问是怎么回事？听差告诉他：“左师爷拜折。”连上奏折他都不知道，湖南巡抚等于左宗棠在做，因而得了个外号，叫做“左邵御史”。巡抚照例挂“右副都御史”衔，叫左宗棠为左都御史，意思是说他比“右副部御史”巡抚的权还要重。
en: Zuo had waited until after Cixi’s birthday before leaving Beijing, with permission to visit his ancestral graves. He reached Changsha, the Hunan provincial capital, on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His first act was to call on Guo Songtao. Their relations were tangled with old favors and grievances. In the eighth year of Xianfeng, when Zuo served on Governor Luo Bingzhang’s staff in Hunan, he decided everything for himself. One day Luo was reading in his office when a gun sounded at the outer gate. As it was not time for the regular noon gun, he asked what had happened. “Adviser Zuo is ceremonially dispatching a memorial,” a servant replied. Luo had not even known that a memorial was being sent. Zuo was virtually the governor of Hunan himself and acquired the nickname “Left Censor-in-Chief.” Governors normally carried the concurrent title of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief: the nickname implied that Zuo exercised still greater power.

zh: 其时有个湖南永州镇总兵樊燮，湖北恩施人，声名不佳，有一次去见左宗棠，谈到永州的防务情形，樊燮一问三不知，而且礼貌上不大周到，左宗棠大为光火，当时甩了他一个大嘴巴，而且立即办了个奏稿，痛劾樊燮“贪纵不法，声名恶劣”，其中有“目不识丁”的考语，也不告诉骆秉章就发出去了。樊燮是否“贪纵不法”，犹待查明，但“目不识丁”何能当总兵官？当下光革职，后查办。这“目不识丁”四字，在樊燮心里，比烙铁烫出来的还要深刻，“解甲归田”以后，好在克扣下来的军饷很不少，当下延聘名师教他的独子读书，书房里“天地君亲师”的木牌旁边，贴一张梅红笺，写的就是“目不识丁”四字。他告诉他的儿子说：“左宗棠不过是个举子，就这么样的神气，你将来不中进士，不是我的儿子。”他这个儿子倒也很争气，后来不但中了迸士，而且点了翰林，早年就是名士，此人就是樊增祥。一方面教子，一方面还要报仇。樊熨走门路，告到骆秉章的上司，两广总督官文那里，又派人进京，在都察院递呈鸣冤。官文为此案出奏，有一句很厉害的话，叫做“一官两印”，意思是说有两个人在做湖南巡抚。名器不可假人，而况是封疆大吏，这件事便很严重了。
en: At that time Fan Xie, brigade commander of Yongzhou in Hunan, was a man of poor reputation from Enshi in Hubei. On one visit, Zuo questioned him about Yongzhou’s defenses. Fan could answer nothing and was less than respectful. Furious, Zuo slapped him hard across the face and immediately drafted a memorial denouncing him as “corrupt, unrestrained, lawless, and notorious.” Among its judgments was “unable to recognize a single written character.” He sent it without informing Luo. Whether Fan was corrupt and lawless remained to be investigated, but how could a wholly illiterate man command a brigade? He was dismissed first and investigated afterward. Those words burned more deeply into him than a branding iron. Once retired, he used the considerable military funds he had withheld to engage distinguished teachers for his only son. Beside the study’s tablet honoring Heaven, Earth, the Sovereign, Parents, and Teachers, he pasted red paper bearing the charge of illiteracy. “Zuo is only a provincial graduate, yet he puts on such airs. Unless you become a jinshi, you are no son of mine.” The son justified his hopes: he not only became a jinshi but entered the Hanlin Academy, winning literary distinction early. He was Fan Zengxiang. While educating his son, Fan also sought revenge. Through influence he appealed to Luo’s superior, Guanwen, described as Governor-General of Liangguang, and sent men to present his grievance at the Censorate in Beijing. Guanwen’s memorial used the formidable phrase “one office, two seals,” meaning that two men were acting as governor of Hunan. Official authority could not be lent to private hands, least of all the authority of a great provincial governor. The matter was serious.

zh: 其时郭嵩焘是南书房翰林，他跟左宗棠的胞兄左宗植是儿女亲家，与左宗棠当然很熟，深知他才气过人，便跟同为南书房的翰林潘祖荫说：“左季高如果不在湖南，一走保不住，东南大局，不夏可问。我跟他同乡，又是姻亲，不便进言，老兄何妨上个摺子。”潘祖荫听他的话，果然上了个摺子，铺叙他的功绩以后，作了个结论：“国家不可一日无湖南，即湖南不可一日无左宗棠。”咸丰一看，为之动容，当即传旨问曾国藩，左宗棠是仍旧在湖南好呢？还是调到曾国藩大营中，以便尽其所长。曾国藩回奏，左宗棠“刚明耐苦，晓畅兵机”。于是奉旨随同曾国藩襄办军务。左宗棠因祸得福，多亏得藩祖荫、郭嵩焘，但他对潘、郭的态度，大不相同。对潘祖荫除了“三节两寿”必送一份极厚的礼金以外，知道潘祖荫好收藏金石碑版，当陕甘总督时，凡是关中有新出土的碑，初拓本一走专差送潘祖荫，有时甚至连原碑都送到潘家。
en: Guo Songtao was then a Hanlin scholar serving in the Southern Study. His child had married a child of Zuo’s elder brother Zuo Zongzhi, so he knew Zuo well and understood his exceptional ability. He approached Pan Zuyin, another Southern Study scholar. “Without Zuo Jigao, Hunan cannot possibly hold out. There would then be no hope for the situation in the southeast. I am his fellow provincial and a relative by marriage; it would be improper for me to speak. Why not submit a memorial yourself?” Pan did so. After recounting Zuo’s achievements, he concluded, “The state cannot do without Hunan for a single day, and Hunan cannot do without Zuo Zongtang for a single day.” Moved, the Xianfeng Emperor asked Zeng Guofan whether Zuo should remain in Hunan or be transferred to his headquarters, where his abilities could be fully used. Zeng replied that Zuo was “firm, clear-sighted, able to endure hardship, and thoroughly versed in military affairs.” An edict assigned him to assist Zeng. Misfortune had become good fortune, thanks largely to Pan and Guo, but Zuo treated the two men very differently. For Pan, he sent generous gifts of money on the customary three festivals and two birthdays. Knowing Pan’s interest in ancient inscriptions and stone monuments, he also sent the first rubbings of newly unearthed Guanzhong steles by special messenger while serving as Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu. Sometimes he sent the original stones themselves.

zh: 郭嵩焘是在洪杨失败后，奉旨出任广东巡抚。两广总督名瑞麟，与巡抚同驻广州，“督抚同城”，常不和睦，瑞麟贪而无能，但为内务府出身，有事可直接诉诸两宫太后，靠山很硬，所以郭嵩焘深受其掣肘之苦而无可如何。那知处境本已很难的郭嵩焘，万想不到多年好友。且曾加以援手的左宗棠会跟他为难，为了协饷，除致函指南以外，且四次上奉祈，指摘郭嵩焘，措施如何不然。郭、左失和的原因，有仲付传说，流传最盛的一个说法是，当郭嵩焘放广东巡抚时，湘阴文庙忽产灵芝，郭嵩焘的胞弟郭昆焘写信给老兄，以为是他开府的吉兆。左宗棠得知其事，大为不悦，说“文庙产灵芝。如果是吉兆，亦当应在我封爵一事上面，与郭家何干？“由此生了意见。其实，湘阴文庙产灵芝，是常有之事，左宗棠亦不至于小气到连这种事都要争，真正的原因是，洪杨军兴以后，带兵大员，就地筹饷，真所谓“有土斯有财”。李鸿章最懂得这个道理，所以始终霸住江苏，尤其是上海这个地盘不放，左宗棠却只得浙江一省，每苦不足，看出广东是大有生发之地。所以狠狠心不顾感情友谊，一再攻讦郭嵩焘。最后终于如愿以偿，由他的大将蒋益澧接了郭嵩焘的手。不过蒋益澧的广东巡抚，干不多久就被调走了。
en: After the Taiping defeat, Guo had been appointed Governor of Guangdong. Ruilin, Governor-General of Liangguang, also resided in Guangzhou. A governor and governor-general in the same city often failed to agree. Ruilin was greedy and incompetent, but his Imperial Household background gave him direct access to both empress dowagers and powerful protection. Guo suffered badly from his obstruction and could do little about it. Difficult though his position already was, he never expected Zuo, an old friend whom he had once helped, to turn against him as well. Over supplementary military contributions, Zuo sent reproachful letters and submitted four memorials criticizing Guo’s administration. Various stories explained their estrangement. The most widespread was that an auspicious lingzhi fungus had appeared in the Confucian temple at Xiangyin when Guo was appointed to Guangdong. His younger brother Guo Kuntao wrote that this foretold good fortune for his new governorship. Zuo supposedly took offense: “If lingzhi in the temple is an omen, it must refer to my ennoblement. What has it to do with the Guo family?” In fact, lingzhi appeared there often, and Zuo was not petty enough to quarrel over such a thing. The real reason lay in military finance. Since the Taiping wars, commanders had raised their own funds: possession of territory meant possession of revenue. Li Hongzhang understood this best and never loosened his grip on Jiangsu, especially Shanghai. Zuo had only Zhejiang, whose resources frequently fell short. Seeing Guangdong’s possibilities, he hardened his heart against friendship and repeatedly attacked Guo. At last his own general, Jiang Yili, replaced him. Jiang’s tenure as Governor of Guangdong, however, was brief; he too was soon transferred.

zh: 郭嵩焘因此郁郁不得志。光绪建元，起用在籍大员，他跟曾国荃同被征召至京，曾国荃放了陕西巡抚，因为不愿与陕甘总督左宗棠共事，改任河东河道总督，郭嵩焘则奉派为福建按察史。这在当过巡抚的人来说，是很委屈的，不过他还是接了事。不久，诏命开缺，以侍郎候补，充任出使英国钦差大臣。其时云南发生英国公使翻译马嘉理，越滇缅边境接应英国武装“探路队”，为中国军民所杀，因而引起的很严重的交涉。英国公使咸妥玛表示，郭嵩焘出使英国，如果在国书上表明中国认错字样，可即赴任，否则应候云南案结后再赴英国。总署诸大臣都认为中国不能认错，郭嵩焘亦就不能出国，奉旨署理兵部侍郎，并在总署行走。
en: Guo remained depressed by his frustrated career. At the beginning of the Guangxu reign, senior officials living in retirement were recalled, and he and Zeng Guoquan were summoned to Beijing. Zeng was appointed Governor of Shaanxi, but, unwilling to serve with Zuo, was transferred to the governor-generalship of the Hedong River Conservancy. Guo became Judicial Commissioner of Fujian. For a former governor, this was humiliating, but he accepted it. Soon afterward he was released from the post, placed on the expectant list for a vice-ministership, and appointed imperial envoy to Britain. At that time the British minister’s interpreter, Margary, had crossed the Yunnan–Burma frontier to meet a British armed surveying party and been killed by Chinese troops and civilians. A serious diplomatic dispute followed. The British minister, Wade, said Guo could leave at once if his credentials acknowledged China’s fault; otherwise he must wait until the Yunnan case was settled. The Zongli Yamen ministers refused such an admission, so Guo could not sail. He was made acting Vice-Minister of War and assigned to the Yamen.

zh: 郭嵩焘对办洋务，一面主张公平合理，认为非此不足以析服洋人。他认为马嘉理被杀一案，云南巡抚岑毓英不能说没有责任，当案发以后，意存掩护，又不查明击杀情由，据实奏报，一味倭罪于深山中的野人。而朝中士大夫又因为官兵所杀的是洋人，群起袒护岑毓英，以至于英国更觉不平，态度亦日趋强硬。郭嵩焘以为，这件纠纷固结不解，全由不讲公平、不讲事理之故，因而奉命入总署之日，便单衔上奏，请旨“将岑毓英先后酿成事端之处，交部严加议处，以为恃虚骄之气，而不务沉心观理、考察详情，以贻累国家者戒。”郭嵩焘平时讲洋务，本已为守旧的“卫道君子”所不满，如今居然参劾杀洋人的岑毓英，在他们看，显然是私通外国，因而引起了公愤，连他平素往来密切的朋友、门生，对他亦很不谅解，湖南则有许多人不认他是同乡。此外京师有人做了一副对联骂他：“出乎其类，拔乎其萃，不容于尧舜之世。未能事人，焉能事鬼，何必去父母之邦？“到得第二年七月底，中英订立《烟台条约》，“滇案”解决。郭嵩焘可以启程赴英国了，当时称为“放洋”，而“放洋”以前又发生了一件很不愉快的事。
en: Guo believed foreign affairs required fairness and reason, without which foreigners could not be persuaded. In his view, Governor Cen Yuying of Yunnan could not disclaim responsibility. After the killing, Cen had sought to protect those involved, failing to establish the circumstances and report them truthfully, and simply blaming remote mountain tribes. Officials at court defended him because the man killed by the troops was a foreigner, making the British feel more wronged and increasingly intransigent. Guo attributed the deadlock entirely to this absence of fairness and reason. On entering the Yamen, he submitted a memorial under his sole name, requesting a strict disciplinary review by the ministry of Cen’s part in provoking the affair, “as a warning to those who rely on empty arrogance instead of calmly examining principles and circumstances, and thereby burden the state.” Conservative defenders of orthodoxy already resented Guo’s views. To impeach a man who had killed foreigners now seemed clear proof of collusion with foreign powers. His action provoked general indignation. Even his close friends and former pupils could not understand him; many Hunan men would no longer acknowledge him as a fellow provincial. In Beijing, someone wrote a mocking couplet: “Outstanding among his kind, surpassing all his fellows—yet unwelcome in an age of Yao and Shun. Unable even to serve men, how can he serve devils? Why must he leave his parents’ land?” At the end of the seventh lunar month of the following year, the Chefoo Convention settled the Yunnan dispute. Guo could finally sail for Britain, but another unhappy incident occurred before his departure.

zh: 有个广东人叫刘锡鸿，原任刑部员外郎，此人是郭嵩焘在广东的旧识，谈起洋务来，颇为投机。此时希望跟郭嵩焘一起放洋。但谈洋务是一回事，办洋务又是一回事，郭嵩焘认为刘锡鸿脾气太刚、好意气用事，而办洋务是“水磨工夫”，颇不相宜。哪知刘锡鸿不死心，托出郭嵩焘的一个好友朱孙治来关说。朱孙治向郭嵩焘说：“你批评他不宜办洋务的话，我都跟他说了，他亦很有自知之明，表示一切不问，你只当带一个可以谈谈，以解异国寂寞的朋友好了。”听得这样说，郭嵩焘可怜刘锡鸿穷困不得意，便上奏保他充任参赞。刘锡鸿是个司员，而且只是六品的员外郎，论资格只能当参赞。不过上谕下来，竟是“刑部员外郎刘锡鸿着即开缺，以五品京堂候补，并加三品衔，充出使英国副使”。这种例子，殊为少见，其中有个内幕，军机大臣李鸿藻对郭嵩焘的态度，有此怀疑，怕他出使后，处处帮英国人讲话，因而提拔刘锡鸿，以副使的身分去钳制正使。这刘锡鸿是个不明事理的人，以为李鸿藻派他去当“打手”，所以谢恩以后，便去看郭嵩焘，责问他为何不保他当副使而当参赞？说他不够朋友，另外还有很难听的话，等于是骂了郭嵩焘一顿。
en: Liu Xihong, a Cantonese formerly serving as an assistant departmental director in the Ministry of Punishments, was an old Guangdong acquaintance with whom Guo had enjoyed discussing foreign affairs. He wanted to accompany him. Talking was one thing, however, and conducting diplomacy another. Guo thought Liu too rigid and impulsive for work requiring patient, delicate effort. Liu persisted, enlisting Guo’s friend Zhu Sunzhi to intercede. Zhu said he had repeated Guo’s criticisms to Liu, who recognized his faults and promised not to meddle: Guo should simply take him as a friend with whom to talk and relieve the loneliness of a foreign country. Moved by Liu’s poverty and lack of prospects, Guo recommended him as a counselor. A mere sixth-rank departmental official, Liu qualified for no higher diplomatic appointment. Yet the edict released him from the Ministry of Punishments, made him an expectant fifth-rank metropolitan court official, added an honorary third-rank title, and appointed him deputy envoy to Britain. Such a precedent was rare. Behind it lay Grand Councillor Li Hongzao’s mistrust of Guo. Fearing that Guo would always take Britain’s side, he had raised Liu to deputy rank to restrain the chief envoy. Liu misunderstood his mission as that of an enforcer. After thanking the throne, he visited Guo and demanded to know why Guo had proposed him only as counselor, rather than deputy envoy. He accused him of failing a friend and added much abusive language.

zh: 郭嵩焘气得半死，总是遇到这种恩将仇报的人，只好自怨命中注定。后来刘锡鸿果然处处跟他为难，而且大吵大闹，不顾体统，郭嵩焘写信给李鸿章，形容共事为“鬼嗥于室，狐啸于梁”，公使馆的上下不安，可想而知。其时刘锡鸿已调充驻德公使，可以单衔上奏，彼此互劾，而由于刘锡鸿有李鸿藻撑腰，占了上风。李鸿藻的门下，赫赫有名的“翰林四谏”之一张佩纶，上奏“请撤回驻英使臣”。郭嵩焘大为泄气，一再求去，终于在光绪五年七月改派曾国藩的长子曾纪泽接替郭嵩焘，不过刘锡鸿亦同时垮台，改派郭嵩焘所欣赏的李凤苞使德。这是李鸿章力争的结果。
en: Guo was furious, but could only blame fate for continually bringing him people who repaid kindness with hostility. Liu indeed obstructed him at every turn and made disgraceful scenes. In a letter to Li Hongzhang, Guo described their service together as “ghosts howling in the rooms, foxes screeching among the rafters.” The unrest throughout the legation was easy to imagine. By then Liu had become minister to Germany and could submit memorials independently. They impeached one another, and Liu’s backing from Li Hongzao gave him the advantage. Zhang Peilun, one of the celebrated Four Hanlin Remonstrants and a follower of Li Hongzao, called for the envoy to Britain to be recalled. Discouraged, Guo repeatedly asked to leave. In the seventh lunar month of Guangxu’s fifth year, Zeng Guofan’s eldest son, Zeng Jize, was appointed to replace him. Liu fell at the same time, however, and Li Fengbao, whom Guo admired, succeeded him in Germany. This was the result of Li Hongzhang’s vigorous intervention.

zh: 郭嵩焘在英国博得极好的声望，所以于郭之去，多表惋惜。郭嵩焘原配早死，继室下堂，只带了个姓梁的姨太太赵英，照她的身分是不能觐见维多利亚女王的，竟亦破例特许。但在英国如此，回国后郭嵩焘自知李鸿藻这班人不会放过他，而且已六十二岁，因而决意引退，一到上海即称病，不回京复命，而请开缺，终得如愿以偿，回湖南后住在长沙。身虽在野，并不消极，关于时政，特别是洋务方面，常跟李鸿章、曾国荃书信往米，细作讨论。日子过得也还闲适。这一年，光绪七年，郭嵩焘年初年尾有两件比较快意之事，一件是二月间，调回国充任通政使司参议的刘锡鸿，因为李鸿章敲掉了他的“洋饭碗”记恨在心，奏劾李鸿章跋扈不臣，俨然帝制。李鸿章正在红的时候，刘锡鸿自不量力，出以此举，自然是自讨没趣，上谕斥责其“信口诬蔑，交部议处”。结果竟落得个革职的处分。
en: Guo had won an excellent reputation in Britain, where his departure was widely regretted. His first wife had long been dead, and his second had been put aside. He had taken only a concubine surnamed Liang to Britain. Her status should have barred an audience with Queen Victoria, yet an exception had been made for her. However well he had been treated there, Guo knew that Li Hongzao’s party would not leave him in peace at home. Already sixty-two, he resolved to retire. On reaching Shanghai he pleaded illness rather than returning to Beijing to report, and requested release from office. His wish was eventually granted, and he settled in Changsha. Retirement did not mean indifference to public affairs. He corresponded frequently with Li Hongzhang and Zeng Guoquan, discussing current policy, especially foreign affairs, in detail. His days were fairly tranquil. In the seventh year of Guangxu, two events, one early and one late, gave him particular satisfaction. In the second lunar month, Liu Xihong, recalled to serve as a councillor in the Office of Transmission, denounced Li Hongzhang as overbearing, disloyal, and practically assuming imperial powers. He resented Li for having broken his diplomatic rice bowl. Li was then at the height of favor, and Liu’s ill-judged attack merely invited humiliation. An edict condemned his “reckless slander” and referred him for disciplinary review. The result was dismissal.

zh: 再一件就是左宗棠来拜访。排场阔极，顶马、跟马高脚牌，前听后拥一顶绿呢大轿，内中坐的是头戴宝石顶、双眼花翎、身穿四开褉袍黄马褂，鼻架一副大墨晶镜的东阁大学士烙靖候。首府长沙知府及首县长沙县，早就在郭嵩焘家附近，清道等候。湖南省的藩、两司、候补道等等，亦来站班。可是郭家双扉紧闭，拒而不纳，左宗棠只好在大门口下轿，由戴红顶子的“材官”上门投帖。“不敢当，不敢当！”郭家门上到左宗棠面前，打千说道：“请大人回驾。”左宗棠早已料到有此一着。一点都不生气，和颜悦色地答说：“你跟你家老爷去回，说我是来看五十年的故人，便衣不恭敬，所以穿了官服来的。”门上一进去，久无消息。首县看“爵相”下不了台，硬闯进去跟郭嵩焘打躬作揖，说是“如果不见，全城文武亦都僵在那里了。”请他体恤下情。总算说动了郭嵩焘，开正门迎接，不过他自己只是站在大厅上等候。“老哥！”左宗棠见面便说：“宗棠无状，特来请罪。”接着，拂一拂马蹄袖，捞起四开褉袍下摆，跪了下去。“不敢，不敢！”郭嵩煮也只好下跪答礼。随从官员，将主客二人都搀扶了起来，左宗棠便自责当年的不是，也不解释是为了军饷，“有土斯有财”的缘故，只连声：“是我该死，是我荒唐。”
en: The other satisfaction was Zuo’s visit. His procession was magnificent: horses before and behind, lofty boards displaying his titles, and crowds of attendants around a great green-covered chair. Within sat the Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and Marquis Kejing, wearing a jeweled hat button, a double-eyed peacock feather, a four-slit robe, and a yellow riding jacket, with large dark crystal spectacles on his nose. The prefect and county magistrate of Changsha had already cleared the streets near Guo’s house and stood waiting. Hunan’s two provincial commissioners, expectant intendants, and other officials also attended. Yet Guo’s double doors remained firmly shut. Zuo had to alight outside and send a red-buttoned military aide with his visiting card. Guo’s doorkeeper came out, made a formal obeisance, and said, “We cannot presume to receive such an honor. Please have Your Excellency’s chair turn back.” Zuo had expected this and showed no anger. “Tell your master that I have come to see a friend of fifty years. Informal clothes would not show sufficient respect, so I have worn my official robes.” The servant went in, and no answer came. Seeing the marquis-grand secretary left in this embarrassing position, the county magistrate forced his way inside and pleaded with Guo: unless he admitted Zuo, all the civil and military officials in the city would remain stranded outside. He begged consideration for their predicament. At last Guo agreed to open the main gate, though he himself waited in the hall. “My old friend,” Zuo said on meeting him, “I behaved disgracefully. I have come expressly to ask your pardon.” He brushed back his horseshoe cuffs, gathered the skirt of his robe, and knelt. “I dare not accept this!” Guo had no choice but to kneel in return. The accompanying officials helped both men up. Zuo reproached himself for his former conduct, making no attempt to explain it by military funding or the need for territory and revenue. He merely repeated, “I deserved to die. I behaved outrageously.”

zh: 左宗棠一向健谈，谈西征、谈边防、谈京里的新闻，又从曾国藩谈起往事，一直到中午都没有告辞的意思，郭嵩焘也不便象督抚会客那样“端茶碗送客”，便只好留饭。随从倒是有首县办差，从长沙第一家大馆子玉楼东去叫了酒席来，在附近的关帝庙接待。左宗棠却必须是郭嵩煮的家庖，才是待客之道。好在湘军出身的达官，除了胡林翼以外，都不甚讲究饮食。左宗棠喜欢吃狗肉，称之为“地羊”，有些一味，加上腊味，再炒一盘去骨的东安鸡，在他便是盛馔了。一顿饭吃到未末申初，左宗棠开始兴尽告辞。临行时做个手势，材官递上一个红封套，左宗棠双手奉上，口中说道：“不腆之仪，聊肋卒岁，务请赏收。”郭嵩焘不肯收，左宗棠非送不可。当着好些湖南的文武官儿，郭嵩焘觉得起了争执，有失体统，便收了下来，不过，心里已经打算好了，拆开封套一看，是阜康钱庄所出的一万两银票，当即提起笔来批上“注销”二字，拿个信封装了，送到左宗棠的行辕。照道理是要回拜的，郭嵩焘也免了这套俗礼。左宗棠到头来，还是讨了个没趣。
en: Zuo was always talkative. He discussed the western campaign, frontier defenses, and news from Beijing, then turned from Zeng Guofan to old times. Noon arrived with no sign of his leaving. Guo could hardly dismiss him by lifting a teacup, as governors did with visitors, and had to invite him to lunch. The county magistrate provided for the attendants, ordering a banquet from Yuloudong, Changsha’s foremost restaurant, to be served at a nearby temple of Guan Di. Zuo, however, must be fed from Guo’s own kitchen if hospitality were to be properly observed. Fortunately, senior men from the Hunan Army, apart from Hu Linyi, were undemanding about food. Zuo liked dog meat, which he called “earth mutton.” A dish of that, some cured meats, and a plate of boned Dong’an chicken made a feast for him. The meal lasted until about three in the afternoon. Only then did his enthusiasm ebb enough for him to leave. At the door he gestured, and a military aide handed him a red envelope. Offering it in both hands, he said, “A modest token to help you through the year’s end. I earnestly beg you to accept it.” Guo refused; Zuo insisted. Before so many Hunan officials, Guo considered a dispute undignified and accepted, having already decided what to do. Inside was a Fukang banknote for ten thousand taels. He immediately wrote “Canceled” across it, put it in another envelope, and sent it to Zuo’s temporary headquarters. Courtesy required a return visit, but Guo dispensed with that convention too. In the end, Zuo had still met with a rebuff.

zh: 十二月初二到湘阴，当天晚上，就收到一道由湖南巡抚衙门派专差送来的军机处的“廷寄”。廷寄中说，有人参劾湖广总督李瀚章“任用私人，纵容劣员，该省防军缺额，虚糜帑金，贻害地方，李瀚章本人默货无套，民怨日深。”原奏肿列了李瀚章许多劣迹，其中情节重大者四款：一，湖北全省厘金，岁收三四百万，报部则仅四万。二，竹木税年收百万，报部仅三万。湖广总督衙门每日用银七百五十两，即在此中开支，年耗帑银二十七万余两。三，以公家轮船，载运私货，公然贩卖。四，李瀚章在扬州、芜湖均设有当铺。清朝的规制，凡是督抚被参，视情节轻重作不同的处置。情节较重者，常由京里特派大员，至少是尚书，且须资格较被参督抚为深的，前往查办。为了防备被参督抚事先湮灭证据，所以明发上谕中只说派某人往某地出差，所谓“某地”决非被参督抚所管的省份，譬如说派到四川出差，湖北是必经之地，一到武昌，立即传旨，随带司员马上动手，封库的封库，查帐的查帐、来他一个措手不及。情节轻微，或者有意把案情看得不重，便就近派官阶资格较高音查办或查夏。左宗棠奉到的上谕是：“将所奏各节，确切查明，据实具奏。”这是查夏，不是查办，可是左宗棠不理这一套。
en: On the second day of the twelfth lunar month, Zuo reached Xiangyin. That evening a special messenger from the governor’s office delivered a confidential dispatch from the Grand Council. It reported an impeachment of Li Hanzhang, Governor-General of Huguang, for employing favorites, indulging corrupt officials, maintaining defense units below their authorized strength while wasting public funds, harming the people, and amassing wealth without restraint. Popular resentment was deepening. Four charges were particularly serious. First, Hubei’s likin revenue amounted to three or four million taels annually, but only forty thousand was reported to the ministry. Second, bamboo and timber duties yielded a million a year, while only thirty thousand was reported. The governor-general’s office spent seven hundred and fifty taels a day from this source, consuming over two hundred and seventy thousand annually. Third, public steamers carried private merchandise for open sale. Fourth, Li owned pawnshops in both Yangzhou and Wuhu. Qing procedure varied according to the gravity of an impeachment against a governor or governor-general. A serious case usually brought a special investigator from Beijing, at least a minister and senior in standing to the accused. To prevent the destruction of evidence, the public edict named another province as his destination. An assignment to Sichuan, for example, required passage through Hubei. On reaching Wuchang, the investigator would proclaim the actual order, and his staff would immediately seal the treasury and inspect the books, taking the accused by surprise. In a minor case, or one the court intended to treat lightly, a nearby official of superior rank and seniority would be appointed to investigate formally or simply ascertain the facts and report. Zuo’s order read, “Establish the truth of each allegation and report the facts.” This was an inquiry for a report, not a formal disciplinary investigation. Zuo disregarded the distinction.

zh: 十二月十三到武昌时，李瀚章已经接到李鸿章的通知，知道左宗棠要来查案，需先示意布政使衔候补道杨宗濂告假回籍。此人在成丰末年，以户部员外郎在原籍江苏金坛办团练。同治元年，江苏土绅凑集了十八万银子，雇用英国轮船到安庆，接淮军到上海打太平军时，杨宗濂就是往来奔走接头的人，以此渊源，与李鸿章的关系很深，李鸿章镇压捻军那两年，杨宗濂替他管过营务处，以后一直在湖北当道员。李氏兄弟相继督鄂，李宗濂由“李二先生”的部属变为“李大先生”的部属，管理汉口“新关”。“关差”一向是好差使，汉口是长江的第一个大码头，收入以竹木税为大宗。西南深山中的木材，以湘西辰州为集散地成“木排”，由阮江入洞庭湖，经岳阳入长江，在汉口交易。宗棠早就听湘西的“排客”谈过，汉口“新关”收竹木税的种种弊端，所以一到武昌，就要找杨宗濂。
en: By the time he reached Wuchang on the thirteenth, Li Hanzhang had been warned by Li Hongzhang that Zuo was coming to investigate. He had prompted Yang Zonglian, an expectant circuit intendant with the honorary title of provincial treasurer, to take leave and return home. In the closing years of Xianfeng, Yang had organized militia in his native Jintan, Jiangsu, while holding rank as an assistant departmental director in the Ministry of Revenue. In Tongzhi’s first year, when Jiangsu gentry raised a hundred and eighty thousand taels to hire British steamers to bring the Anhui Army from Anqing to fight the Taipings at Shanghai, Yang had gone back and forth making the arrangements. This gave him a close connection with Li Hongzhang. During Li’s two years fighting the Nian, Yang had managed his army administration; afterward he remained a circuit intendant in Hubei. As the Li brothers successively governed the province, he passed from the service of “Second Master Li” to that of “Eldest Master Li,” managing Hankou’s New Customs. A customs assignment was always lucrative. Hankou was the Yangtze’s foremost commercial port, and bamboo and timber duties formed its principal customs revenue. Timber from the southwestern mountains was assembled into rafts at Chenzhou in western Hunan, floated down the Ruan River into Dongting Lake, then through Yueyang to the Yangtze for sale at Hankou. Zuo had long heard western Hunan raft merchants describe abuses at the New Customs. On reaching Wuchang, he immediately sought Yang.

zh: 由于奉旨查案，所以左宗棠跟李瀚章不作私人的交往，在行辕以一角公文咨湖广总督衙门，“请饬杨宗濂到案备询”，而夏文是“该员业已告假回籍，无从传饬”。这一下左宗棠大为光火，用“札子”下给汉黄德道及武昌府，“催令杨宗濂迅赴江宁问话“。一面出奏：”臣前次回湘，路过新关，杨宗濂避而未见，此次又先朗告假回籍，是否有意规避，虽未可知，而查询杨宗濂素日声名平常、性情浮动，则众论相同，无代其剖白者。“至于经收竹木税有无弊端，”应俟查取票根底薄，传杨宗濂到到案质询，方昭核实“。接着声明：因为须赴两江接任，所以传杨宗濂到江宁备询，同时以”贪鄙狄诈“的考语，请旨将杨宗濂”先行革职，听候查办“。此外汉黄德道何维键、候补知府李谦，都是李瀚章的私人，左宗棠亦毫不客气，对何维键以“庸软无能”四字考语，奏请“开缺送部引见”，意思是请慈禧太后亲自考查，对李谦则谓之“性善圆通、难期振作”，请旨交湖北巡抚彭祖贤“察看”。
en: Acting under an imperial commission, Zuo avoided private dealings with Li Hanzhang. From his temporary headquarters he sent the governor-general’s office a formal request that Yang be ordered to attend for questioning. The reply stated that Yang had already taken leave and returned home, and could not be summoned. Zuo was furious. He issued directives to the Han–Huang–De circuit intendant and the prefect of Wuchang, requiring them to have Yang proceed promptly to Jiangning for questioning. He also memorialized: “On my previous journey home through the New Customs, Yang Zonglian avoided meeting me. On this occasion he again obtained leave in advance and returned home. Whether this was deliberate evasion cannot yet be known. Inquiries into his ordinary reputation, however, agree that it is undistinguished and his disposition unstable. No one speaks in his defense.” Whether there had been fraud in the bamboo and timber duties must await examination of the receipt counterfoils and original ledgers, together with Yang’s personal interrogation. Zuo explained that, as he had to assume office in Liangjiang, Yang was being summoned to Jiangning. Describing him as “greedy, mean, and deceitful,” he requested Yang’s immediate dismissal pending investigation. He Weijian, the circuit intendant, and Li Qian, an expectant prefect, were also Li Hanzhang’s clients. Zuo spared neither. Calling He “weak and incompetent,” he requested removal from his post and presentation through the ministry for an imperial audience—in other words, examination by Cixi herself. Li Qian was “adept at accommodating himself to others, unlikely to show vigor.” Zuo asked that Governor Peng Zuxian of Hubei keep him under observation.

zh: 奏折中还将李瀚章训了一顿，他说：李瀚章一门，遭逢圣时，功名大显，亲党交游，能自立的亦颇不乏人。不过依附者亦很多，当时随从立功，身致富贵者，又各有其亲友，辗转依附，久而久之，恃势妄为，官府处置为难，不能不作姑息，乡里受其欺凌，亦惟有敢怒而不敢言。由于“贤者不肯规之以正，懦者畏其忌嫉，谣诼纷兴、事端叠起，洵非家门之福。宜以身作则，毋与乡邦人士争势竟利，遇事敛抑，免为怨府。其李鸿章、李瀚章所难尽言者，臣等忝仕疆圻，亦当尽心化诲，俾知以义为利，如思保世承家，为报国之本，则李氏亲友之福，亦李鸿章、李瀚章一门之福也”。话说得很不客气，但左宗棠自以为对李瀚章多所开脱，帮了他很大的忙。十二月十九拜发奏折以后，随即坐长江轮船，鼓悼东下，到江宁拜印接任。因为如此，使得胡雪岩扑了个空。原来左宗棠原先的计划是：回湖南原籍祭祖扫墓以后，南下由广东至福建，自厦门坐特派的南洋兵舰到上海，再转江宁接任。这是为了一履旧日百战立功之地，同时还有“南洋大臣”巡海之意。不想一到湘阴，有奉旨查夏李瀚章纵容劣员一案，前后耽误了十一天，不能不走捷径，在年前赶到江宁接任。
en: The memorial also lectured Li Hanzhang. The Li family, Zuo wrote, had enjoyed an enlightened reign and risen to great distinction. Many relatives and associates could support themselves, but many others lived through dependence. Those who had earned wealth and rank in the brothers’ service had their own friends and relations, creating successive chains of patronage. In time such people abused their influence. Officials found them difficult to punish and tolerated them; local people endured their bullying, angry but afraid to speak. “The worthy will not correct them, while the timid fear their resentment. Slanders multiply and troubles arise one after another. This can scarcely benefit the family. They should lead by example, refrain from contending with their fellow provincials for power and profit, and exercise restraint, lest they become a focus of resentment. Where Li Hongzhang and Li Hanzhang cannot say everything necessary, we who have the honor to hold provincial office should earnestly instruct these people, so they may understand that righteousness is their true advantage. Preserving the family across generations is the foundation of service to the state. Such conduct would benefit both the Li brothers’ relatives and friends and the family itself.” The language was far from gentle, yet Zuo believed he had largely exonerated Li and done him a great service. After ceremonially dispatching the memorial on the nineteenth day of the twelfth month, he took a Yangtze steamer east to Jiangning to receive the seal and assume office. Thus Hu’s journey to meet him came to nothing. Zuo’s original plan had been to visit the ancestral graves, then travel south through Guangdong to Fujian, take a specially dispatched Nanyang warship from Xiamen to Shanghai, and proceed to Jiangning. Besides revisiting the ground of his old campaigns, he intended a coastal inspection in his capacity as Nanyang Minister. The imperial inquiry received at Xiangyin delayed him eleven days, forcing him to take the direct route if he was to assume office before the new year.

zh: “既在如此，小爷叔你回杭州过年吧。”古应春说：“过了年，我陪小爷叔专程到南京去一趟。”“也只好这样子。不过，七姐的病，我实在不放心。”“不要紧的。人是醒过来了，只要慢慢调养，逐渐会好的。医生说：中风这种病，全靠调理。将来总归带病延年了。”胡雪岩跟七姑奶奶情如兄妹，看她人虽醒了，却还不能说话，不过人是认得的，一见双泪交流，嘴唇翕动，不知多少有苦难言，胡雪岩忍不住也掉眼泪。“小爷叔，小爷叔，千万不要如此。”古应春劝道：“这样子反让病人心里难过。”胡雪岩点点头，抹掉眼泪，强作欢颜，坐在病榻前向七姑奶奶说道：“七姐，年底下事情太多，我不能不走。你慢慢调养，我记得你的八字上，说你四十四岁有一关，来势虽凶，凶而不险，过了这一关，寿至七十八。今年年内春，算壬午年，你正好四十四，你这一关应过了，明年秋天，老太太等你来吃寿酒。”七姑奶奶口不能言，却听得懂，只在枕上摆头，表示会意。“还有句，七姐，那种荒唐事情，偶尔一回，以后决不会再做了。”七姑奶奶致疾之由，便是由于气恼胡雪岩的荒唐，所以这句对她是最好的安慰，居然含着泪笑了。
en: “In that case, Little Uncle, go home to Hangzhou for the new year,” Gu said. “Afterward I shall accompany you on a special visit to Nanjing.” “There seems no other choice. But I cannot stop worrying about Seventh Sister.” “She will be all right. She has regained consciousness; with patient nursing she will gradually improve. The doctor says a stroke depends above all on aftercare. She will have to live on with the illness.” Hu and the Seventh Lady were as close as brother and sister. Though awake, she still could not speak. She recognized him, and tears streamed down her face as her lips moved, full of things she could not say. Hu could not hold back his own tears. “Little Uncle, please do not,” Gu urged. “That only makes her feel worse.” Hu nodded, wiped his eyes, and forced a cheerful expression. Sitting beside the bed, he said, “Seventh Sister, there is so much business at year’s end that I must leave. Take time to recover. I remember your horoscope said you would meet a crisis at forty-four: fierce in its onset, but not truly dangerous. Once past it, you would live to seventy-eight. This year the Beginning of Spring falls before the lunar year ends, so the reckoning is already the renwu year, when you turn forty-four. You have passed the crisis. Next autumn Mother will be waiting for you at her birthday feast.” Unable to speak but understanding him, she moved her head on the pillow to acknowledge his words. “One more thing, Seventh Sister. That foolish conduct was a single lapse. It will never happen again.” Anger at his behavior had brought on her illness, and this was the best comfort he could offer. She even smiled through her tears.

zh: 离了病榻，打点回乡。当天晚上，古应春为胡雪岩饯行，只为七姑奶奶在病中，所以在家由厨娘备了几味精致的肴馔，也不邀陪客，只是两人对酌。在餐桌上，采运局的司事送来了一封信，是左宗棠自湘阴所发，告诉胡雪岩因为奉旨赴武昌办案，原来的行程取消，武昌事毕，径赴江宁，约胡雪岩灯节以后，在江宁相会。此外又托胡雪岩查一件事，说是“江苏司关厘局，及鄂湘皖西的督销局，每月均有专拨之饷。其细数如何，乞为密访见示。”胡雪岩看完信，沉吟了好一会说：“我看，左大人对李合肥要动手了。”“喔，小爷叔看出苗头来了？”古应春问道：“怎么样动手法？”“这还言之过早。而且动手也要看机会，不过左大人现在已经有这个意思了。”
en: Leaving her bedside, Hu prepared to return home. Gu gave him a farewell dinner that evening. With the Seventh Lady ill, they stayed at home, where the cook prepared a few delicate dishes. No other guests were invited; the two men drank alone. During dinner a clerk from the Purchasing and Transport Bureau brought a letter from Zuo, written at Xiangyin. It explained that the imperial order to investigate at Wuchang had canceled his original itinerary. When that business was finished, he would go straight to Jiangning, and wished to meet Hu there after the Lantern Festival. He also requested a discreet inquiry: “The treasury, customs, likin and other bureaus in Jiangsu, together with the salt-sales supervision bureaus in Hubei, Hunan, Anhui and the province abbreviated as Xi, all make earmarked monthly military remittances. What are the exact amounts? Pray inquire confidentially and let me know.” Hu considered the letter for some time. “I believe His Excellency means to move against Li of Hefei.” “You see a sign of it, Little Uncle? How will he act?” “It is too early to say, and action will depend on opportunity. But he already has the intention.”

zh: 原来李鸿章的准军有好些部队，驻扎在江苏，湘淮军都是子弟兵，行命将，后招募，募兵成营，即以统率将官之名命名。吴长庆所部名“庆字营”，有一营在江苏，“刘六麻子”刘铭传虽已挟其宦囊，在合肥原籍构筑“大潜山房”，饮酒赋诗，大过儒将的瘾，但“铭字营”的番号依旧，不过由李鸿章拿他们一分为二，一部分由记名提督刘盛休统带，驻山东张秋一带，防守运河要口，一部分交福建提督唐定奎率领，驻防江苏、靖江两县，另有铭字先锋马队之营，驻扎江苏宿迁，主要的任务，亦是防运河沿岸一带有警，可以迅速赴援。李鸿章的淮军中。亦有原为湘军的将领，此人名叫郭松林，他的旧部名为“武毅军”，有十营为江防军，亦驻江阴、靖江境内，有五营为海防军，驻扎上海、宝山两县境内。这些部队，都由江苏发饷。所谓“司关厘局”，司指藩局，关指海关，厘指厘金，局指捐局、税局以及淮盐督销局。两淮出盐，盐课收入为两江一大财源。但上江安徽、下江江苏两省的人吃不完两淮的盐，所以淮盐有指定的销售地区，称为“引局”，分布在鄂、湘、西、皖四个省份，西非山西而是江西。这四省都有淮盐督销局，收入亦归两江。
en: Several units of Li’s Anhui Army were stationed in Jiangsu. Like the Hunan Army, it consisted of men recruited through personal and local ties. A commander was appointed first and then raised his men; the resulting camps took his name. Wu Changqing’s forces were the Qing camps, one of which was stationed in Jiangsu. Although “Sixth Pockmarked Liu,” Liu Mingchuan, had already carried home his official fortune and built the Daqian Mountain Retreat at Hefei, where he drank, wrote poetry, and thoroughly enjoyed playing the scholarly general, the Ming camps retained their designation. Li had divided them. One part, under Liu Shengxiu, a registered candidate for provincial military command, guarded important canal points around Zhangqiu in Shandong. Another, under Tang Dingkui, the provincial military commander of Fujian, was stationed in two counties named in the text as Jiangsu and Jingjiang. A mounted vanguard camp of the Ming forces stood at Suqian in Jiangsu, chiefly to rush to the aid of places along the canal at the first alarm. The Anhui Army also included a former Hunan Army commander, Guo Songlin. His old forces were known as the Wuyi Army. Ten camps formed river-defense units in Jiangyin and Jingjiang, while five served coastal defense in Shanghai and Baoshan. Jiangsu paid all these troops. The expression “treasury, customs, likin and bureaus” meant the provincial treasury, customs offices, likin administration, contribution and tax bureaus, and the Huai Salt Sales Supervision Bureau. Salt from Lianghuai was an important source of revenue for Liangjiang. Anhui and Jiangsu could not consume the entire output, so designated sales areas, known as salt-certificate districts, extended into Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, and Anhui. Here Xi meant Jiangxi, not Shanxi. Each of the four provinces had a Huai Salt Sales Supervision Bureau, whose revenue also belonged to Liangjiang.

zh: “也不回杭州查，也不叫采运局去办，我有个极方便的法子叫老宓写信到各处问一问，就差不多了。”胡雪岩口中的“老宓”，名叫宓本常，宁波人，他是阜丰雪记沪庄的档手。沪庄是阜丰总号，由他分函各地阜丰联号一查“司关厘局”近几个月汇款到淮军后路粮台的数目，每个月的负担，大致就可以算出来了，确是个很方便的办法。“不过，”古应春说：“既然左大人是要攻李合肥，这件事就是隐秘，这样子做法，会不会有风声传出去？”“ 有啥风声传出去？”胡雪岩说：“譬如，你是南昌阜丰的档手，我问你江西淮盐督销局每个月汇到江宁淮军后路粮台的款子有多少？你怎么会想到这是左大人要查了有作用的？”“不错，不错。我是知道了有这么件事，才会顾虑，不知道，我做梦也想不到的。不过，小爷叔，既然各处都是汇到江宁，那又何必费事，只要江宁阜丰查一查，总帐不就出来了？”“啊！啊！”胡雪岩在自己额头上拍了一下，“脑筋不灵了！‘脱裤子放屁’，真是多余的。“于是第二天在上船之前，胡雪岩就办好了这件事，只不过写两封信，一封是写给左宗棠，说江苏各处解交淮军后路粮台的款项，似乎除了委托阜丰以外，另无更简易的通汇之法，所以已函江宁阜丰开单径呈辕门，如有缺漏，另再设法查报。此外叙明，准明年灯节以后，到江宁叩遏。一封是写给江宁阜丰的档手，照办其事。
en: “There is no need to investigate in Hangzhou or set the Purchasing and Transport Bureau to work,” Hu said. “I have a much easier way. Let Old Mi write to the various places and ask. That should tell us nearly everything.” Old Mi was Mi Benchang of Ningbo, manager of the Shanghai establishment of Fufeng Xueji Bank. Shanghai was Fufeng’s headquarters. If he wrote to its affiliated banks in the various places, asking how much the treasury, customs, and other offices had remitted in recent months to the Anhui Army’s Rear Commissariat, the approximate monthly burden could readily be calculated. It was indeed convenient. “But if His Excellency intends to attack Li, the inquiry must be secret,” Gu said. “Might word of it get out?” “What word? Suppose you managed Fufeng at Nanchang. If I asked how much the Jiangxi Huai Salt Sales Supervision Bureau sent each month to the Rear Commissariat at Jiangning, why would you imagine that Zuo wanted the figures for a particular purpose?” “Quite right. I worry only because I know what lies behind it. Otherwise I should never dream of it. But if all the money goes to Jiangning, why take so much trouble? Have the Fufeng bank there look it up. Would that not give us the total account?” “Ah!” Hu slapped his forehead. “My brain is failing me. Taking off my trousers to fart—quite unnecessary!” Before boarding the boat next morning, he had set the matter in motion with just two letters. One informed Zuo that there seemed to be no simpler way of remitting the Jiangsu offices’ military contributions than through Fufeng. Hu had therefore asked its Jiangning manager to prepare a statement and send it directly to Zuo’s headquarters; any omissions could be investigated and reported afterward. He also confirmed that he would come after the Lantern Festival. The second letter instructed the Jiangning manager to carry this out.

zh: “小爷叔，”古应春问：“开年什么时候来？”“总在上灯前后。”“好！到时候我陪小爷叔一起到南京。”“我当然巴不得你陪了我去，不过，也要看七姐的情形。”“那时候一定不要紧了。”古应春又说：“阿七得病，小爷叔回去了不必提。过年了，何必让老太太记挂。”胡雪岩不答，沉吟了好一会，叹口气说：“我实在没有想到，七姐为了我，会这样子在意。”古应春欲言又止，考虑了一会，终于说了出来，“小爷叔，既然你看出来了，我索性就说吧！阿七为小爷叔担心，也不是一天两天的事了。她常说：树大招风。小爷叔无心结下的怨家，大概不少。这倒还在其次，这几年小爷叔用的人，大不如前，有的本事有限，有的品性不好。她说，她还真不知道小爷叔的眼光，为啥不大灵了？是事情太多太杂，还是精神不济，照顾不到，或者是别有缘故？”胡雪岩脸一红，心知道“别有缘故”四字，是古应春说得含蓄，这“缘故”，说来说去总由于狗皮膏药在作怪。“七姐为我好，我晓得。不过，她实在也担心得稍微过头了。”胡雪岩又说：“等七姐稍微好一点，你同她说：她说我的毛病，我要仔仔细细想一想，结结实实拿它改掉。”“小爷叔这么说，阿七心里一定宽得多。”古应春欣然答说。
en: “When will you come back after the new year, Little Uncle?” Gu asked. “Around the time the lanterns go up.” “Good. I shall go to Nanjing with you then.” “Nothing would please me better, but it depends on Seventh Sister’s condition.” “She is sure to be well enough by then. And when you go home, do not mention A’qi’s illness. With the new year coming, why make your mother worry?” Hu was silent for some time. At last he sighed. “I truly never imagined Seventh Sister would care so deeply about what happened to me.” Gu hesitated, then decided to speak. “Since you have seen it, Little Uncle, I may as well say so. A’qi has been worrying about you for a long time. She often says a tall tree catches the wind. You must have made many enemies without intending to. That is the lesser concern. In recent years, the people you employ have been much poorer than before: some lack ability, others character. She cannot understand why your judgment has grown less sharp. Is your business too extensive and complicated? Have you less energy to oversee it? Or is there some other reason?” Hu flushed. He knew “some other reason” was Gu’s discreet way of putting it. In the end, the trouble came back to the dogskin plasters. “I know Seventh Sister means well. But she does worry rather more than she need. When she is a little better, tell her I shall think very carefully about every fault she has pointed out and make a thorough effort to correct it.” “That will put A’qi’s mind much more at ease,” Gu replied with pleasure.
